title: Collect Errors
prompt: A TypeScript import job returns successful and failed rows. Write a function that returns only the error messages from failed rows, preserving their original order.

explanation.beginner:
Example: collectErrors([{"ok":true,"id":"1"},{"ok":false,"error":"Missing name"}]) produces ["Missing name"]. Check each independent constraint and associate failures with the field or rule that caused them.

Compare “returns empty for all successful rows”: input [[{"ok":true,"id":"1"}]] produces []. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Check each independent constraint and associate failures with the field or rule that caused them.

Tempting mistake: Returning at the first error may hide other errors when the contract asks for all of them. Whitespace and empty strings need explicit treatment.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “returns empty for all successful rows”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
